title: Direct Identification via Government ID
description: Government ID and name data collected during parent registration can directly identify the individual, creating identification privacy risks.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Email, password, name, government ID, and six-digit code could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities or insider threats.

title: Linkability of Registration Data to Other Records
description: Registration data could be linked to other data sources (e.g., other services, databases) creating comprehensive user profiles.

title: Data Degradation of Sensitive Information
description: Government ID and password data could be corrupted, altered, or degraded during processing or storage.

title: Unauthorized access to parent account data
description: MongoDB users collection storing parent account information may be accessible to unauthorized parties through database vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, or insufficient access controls.

title: Identification of users from parent account data
description: Parent account information stored in the authentication service could be used to identify specific individuals, potentially revealing personal relationships or family structures.

title: Unauthorized modification of parent account data
description: Parent account information in MongoDB could be modified by attackers, potentially altering authentication credentials or user relationships.

title: Impersonation using parent account credentials
description: Parent account authentication data could be stolen and used by attackers to impersonate legitimate users or gain unauthorized access to parent accounts.

title: User Identifiability via JWT and User Data
description: The JWT token and associated user data transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User can directly identify the parent user, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized parties if intercepted or mishandled.
assumptions: JWT contains identifiable user information; data transmission is not fully encrypted or protected

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of User Data
description: User data transmitted in the JWT could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through network interception, insider threats, or improper access controls at the Authentication Service.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be fully secured; access controls may be insufficient

title: JWT Token Usurpation and Impersonation
description: An attacker who obtains the JWT token could potentially impersonate the parent user by presenting the token to the Authentication Service or other systems that trust it, leading to unauthorized access.
assumptions: JWT is not properly validated; token may be transmitted or stored insecurely

title: Linkability of User Data Across Sessions
description: The JWT and user data could be linked across multiple sessions or with other data sources, enabling profiling or tracking of the parent user's activities and behavior patterns.
assumptions: User data contains consistent identifiers; data is not properly anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Excessive Data Collection by Parent User
description: The Parent User may receive more user data than necessary for the authentication context, potentially violating data minimization principles and exposing unnecessary personal information.
assumptions: Parent User may not have proper controls to limit data received; data scope may be overly broad

title: Linkability of Child's Login Activity to Parent Identity
description: The child's login activity using parent credentials could be linked to the parent's identity, creating a connection between the child's online activities and the parent's personal information.
assumptions: Parent credentials are used for child authentication, and login logs are retained.

title: Direct Identification of Child User
description: The child's identity could be directly identified through the login process, especially since they're using parent credentials, making the child identifiable in the system.
assumptions: Login records are stored and accessible.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Parent Credentials
description: The parent email and password transmitted during child login could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to credential disclosure.
assumptions: Transmission may not be fully encrypted or credentials could be logged.

title: Tampering with Login Credentials
description: The login credentials could be tampered with during transmission, leading to authentication bypass or unauthorized access.
assumptions: Data in transit could be intercepted and modified.

title: Usurpation of Child's Identity
description: Someone else could potentially usurp the child's identity by gaining access to the parent credentials, allowing unauthorized access to child-specific services.
assumptions: Parent credentials could be compromised or shared.

title: Child User Identifiability via JWT and Profiles
description: The JWT token and child profiles transmitted from the Authentication Service contain personally identifiable information that can be used to identify the child user across systems and contexts.
assumptions: JWT tokens and child profiles contain unique identifiers or quasi-identifiers that can be linked to the child user.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child profiles may contain sensitive personal information (e.g., health data, location, family information) that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the JWT is compromised or intercepted during transmission.
assumptions: Child profiles contain sensitive PII; JWT tokens can be intercepted or stolen.

title: JWT Token Theft and User Impersonation
description: JWT tokens transmitted from the Authentication Service could be stolen or intercepted, allowing an attacker to impersonate the child user and access their profile data or perform actions on their behalf.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted over networks where interception is possible; tokens may not have adequate expiration or revocation mechanisms.

title: Excessive Data Collection in Child Profiles
description: Child profiles may contain more personal data than necessary for the authentication service's legitimate purpose, violating data minimization principles and increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Child profiles include fields not strictly required for authentication or service delivery.

title: Non-compliance with Child Data Protection Regulations
description: Handling child user data (JWT and profiles) may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy laws if appropriate consent, parental controls, or data protection measures are not implemented.
assumptions: The system processes data of children under 13/16 depending on jurisdiction; regulations require specific protections for child data.

title: Linkability of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data (name, DOB, gender, government ID) could be linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's identity and background.
assumptions: Data is stored in systems that can be cross-referenced with external databases

title: Direct Identification of Child
description: The combination of government ID, name, and date of birth enables direct identification of the child, creating privacy risks if this information is exposed.
assumptions: Government ID is unique and can be used to identify the child

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Data
description: Sensitive child profile information including government ID could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or system vulnerabilities exist

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: Child profile data could be tampered with, modified, or corrupted by unauthorized actors, leading to incorrect or fraudulent information being associated with the child.
assumptions: Insufficient data integrity controls or authentication mechanisms

title: Child Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate the child to create a fraudulent profile using stolen or fabricated information, potentially leading to identity theft or unauthorized access.
assumptions: Parent user credentials are compromised or insufficient verification exists

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Collection and processing of child profile data may violate child protection regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding consent, data minimization, and parental rights.
assumptions: Data processing practices may not fully comply with applicable child protection laws

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB may be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, leading to privacy violations of minors' personal information.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or enforced

title: Malicious manipulation of child profile data
description: Child profile information could be tampered with by unauthorized actors, leading to false or altered records that could impact the child's welfare or legal status.
assumptions: Data integrity controls are insufficient

title: Unauthorized identification of children
description: Child profile data may be used to identify minors without proper consent or legal basis, violating privacy rights of children.
assumptions: Data is accessible to unauthorized entities

title: Linkability of child profile data with other datasets
description: Child profile information could be linked with other data sources (e.g., parent data, medical records) to create comprehensive profiles without consent.
assumptions: Data can be correlated across systems

title: Usurpation of child identity
description: Unauthorized actors could impersonate children or parents to access or modify child profile data, potentially leading to fraudulent activities.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Storage and processing of child profile data may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy laws.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements are not fully addressed in system design

title: Linkability of Video Search and Interaction Patterns
description: Child User's video search queries, likes, and comments can be linked across sessions and contexts, potentially revealing user interests, preferences, and behavioral patterns that could be used to build a profile.
assumptions: System logs and stores search/interaction history with user identifiers

title: Identification Through Video Preferences and Comments
description: Video search patterns, liked content, and comments may contain or reveal personally identifiable information, allowing the user to be identified from their interaction data.
assumptions: Comments may contain PII; search patterns are unique enough to identify users

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Content and Interaction Data
description: Video content, search history, likes, and comments may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities exist

title: Excessive Collection of Video Interaction Data
description: Video Management Service may collect more data than necessary for the stated purpose (video search, request, like, comment), including detailed interaction logs that exceed privacy expectations.
assumptions: System collects comprehensive logs of all user interactions

title: Usurpation Through Account Compromise
description: Child User's account could be compromised, allowing an attacker to access video content, perform actions on behalf of the user, and potentially impersonate them.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to attacks

title: Regulatory Compliance Violations for Video and Comment Data
description: Video content and user comments may be subject to data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) that require specific handling, consent, and retention policies that may not be properly implemented.
assumptions: System may not fully comply with applicable privacy regulations

title: Video metadata linkability to individuals
description: Video metadata (timestamps, locations, device IDs) could be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking of movements and activities across time and space.
assumptions: Metadata contains or can be correlated with identifying information

title: Video content reveals identifiable individuals
description: Video files may contain visual or audio content that identifies individuals (faces, voices, activities), potentially exposing personal information without consent.
assumptions: Videos capture identifiable people in private or semi-private settings

title: Unauthorized access to video files and metadata
description: MongoDB data store may be accessible by unauthorized parties, leading to exposure of video content and associated metadata to individuals without proper authorization.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities in MongoDB

title: Unauthorized video upload or retrieval
description: Malicious or compromised users could upload videos containing others' images or retrieve videos they should not access, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Authentication/authorization mechanisms are insufficient

title: GDPR compliance violations with video data
description: Storage and processing of video metadata and files may violate GDPR requirements for consent, data minimization, and right to erasure, especially for biometric data.
assumptions: Video data qualifies as personal/biometric data under GDPR

title: Child Identifiability from Search/Watch History
description: Search and watch history stored in child profiles could be used to identify the child's identity, interests, and behavioral patterns, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about the child.
assumptions: The data is stored in a manner that allows correlation with other identifying information
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a general identifiability node; specific LINDDUN Pro tree structure may vary

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child search and watch history could be disclosed to unauthorized parties including other users, third-party services, or even unauthorized family members without proper consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific context may require different sub-node

title: Linkability of Child Data Across Systems
description: Child search and watch history could be linked with other data sources (e.g., parental accounts, device identifiers, location data) to create comprehensive profiles of the child's activities and preferences.
assumptions: Data exists in multiple systems that can be correlated
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific threat-tree structure may vary

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Child History
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection storing search and watch history could be tampered with, altered, or deleted by unauthorized actors, potentially corrupting the child's activity records.
assumptions: The data store lacks adequate integrity controls and access restrictions
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a general data integrity node; specific LINDDUN Pro tree may have different structure

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Children's Data
description: Storing child search and watch history may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other child privacy regulations regarding data minimization, parental consent, and data retention requirements.
assumptions: Data collection and storage practices do not meet applicable legal requirements for children's data
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is a general non-compliance node; specific regulatory context may require different classification

title: Video Content Identifies User
description: Video data inherently contains identifiable information about the user, including facial features, voice, and personal context, making the user directly identifiable from the uploaded content.

title: Unauthorized Video Disclosure
description: Video data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during storage, processing, or transmission within the Video Management Service, potentially exposing sensitive personal information.

title: Video Data Tampering
description: Video data could be altered or tampered with during the upload or approval/rejection process, compromising data integrity and potentially creating false evidence.

title: Cross-Context Linkability
description: Video data could be linked to the user across different systems or time periods, enabling profiling and tracking of user behavior beyond the immediate context.

title: Approval Process Usability Issues
description: The approval/rejection process may be difficult to use or understand, potentially leading to privacy-related errors or user frustration that could result in unintended data exposure.

title: Child Identifiable from Video Stream
description: The video stream contains visual content that can identify the child user, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized observers.

title: Video Stream Disclosure to Unauthorized Parties
description: The video stream could be intercepted, recorded, or accessed by unauthorized third parties during transmission or storage.

title: Video Stream Linkable to Child Identity
description: The video content can be linked to the child's identity through metadata, timestamps, or contextual information, enabling profiling.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Children's Privacy Laws
description: Streaming video to a child may violate regulations such as COPPA or GDPR-K regarding children's data protection and consent requirements.

title: Child Identifiability from Profile Data
description: Child profiles in MongoDB collection contain personally identifiable information that could directly or indirectly identify children, violating privacy expectations for minors.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Browsing Data
description: Child browsing data could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, leading to privacy violations and potential exploitation.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: Child data processing may violate COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy regulations due to insufficient consent mechanisms and data protection measures.

title: Linkability of Child Data Across Systems
description: AI Recommendation Engine could link child browsing data with other datasets, creating comprehensive profiles that increase identifiability risks.

title: Unauthorized Use of Child Data for AI Training
description: Child browsing data could be used to train AI models without proper parental consent, violating child privacy rights and regulatory requirements.

title: AI-Generated Misleading Recommendations
description: AI Recommendation Engine could generate manipulative or age-inappropriate content recommendations based on child browsing patterns, deceiving children about content suitability.

title: Linkability of browsing data to individual users
description: Browsing data sent to third-party advertisers may be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking across sessions and devices.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to additional identifiers that can correlate browsing data with user identities.

title: Identifiability of users from browsing patterns
description: Browsing data can be used to infer or directly identify individual users, revealing personal interests, habits, and potentially sensitive information.
assumptions: Advertisers can analyze browsing patterns to build user profiles that identify individuals.

title: Over-disclosure of browsing data to advertisers
description: More browsing data may be shared with advertisers than necessary for the intended purpose, exposing users to unnecessary privacy risks.
assumptions: Data minimization principles are not followed; excessive data is transmitted.

title: Deception about data usage and purposes
description: Users may not be fully informed about how their browsing data will be used by third-party advertisers, leading to consent without understanding.
assumptions: Privacy policies are unclear or users do not read them; data usage extends beyond stated purposes.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent and safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for third-party data sharing are not met; consent mechanisms are inadequate.

title: Direct Identification of Data Subjects
description: Government ID images contain personally identifiable information that directly identifies individuals, making them highly sensitive to identification attacks.

title: Linkability of ID Images to Other Data Sources
description: Stored government ID images can be linked to other datasets (e.g., transaction records, biometric data) creating comprehensive profiles of individuals.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of ID Images
description: File system storing government ID images may be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities.

title: Data Manipulation of Stored ID Images
description: ID images in the file system could be altered, tampered with, or replaced by malicious actors compromising data integrity.

title: Identity Usurpation via Stolen ID Images
description: If ID images are compromised, attackers could use them to impersonate individuals and gain unauthorized access to systems or services.

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Storing government ID images may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations requiring strict handling of sensitive personal identification data.

title: JWT Token Disclosure via XSS
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage are accessible to any JavaScript running on the page, making them vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. An attacker with XSS access can read and exfiltrate the JWT token.
assumptions: Vulnerable to XSS due to localStorage accessibility

title: Session Hijacking via Stolen JWT
description: If a JWT token is stolen from localStorage (e.g., via XSS, network sniffing, or malicious browser extension), an attacker can use it to impersonate the authenticated user and gain unauthorized access to protected resources.
assumptions: JWT contains valid authentication claims and is not short-lived

title: User Identifiability from JWT Claims
description: JWT tokens often contain user identifiers (sub, email, user_id) in their claims. If exposed, these can be used to identify and profile the user across systems.
assumptions: JWT contains identifiable user information in claims

title: JWT Token Tampering
description: Since localStorage is mutable via JavaScript, an attacker with access can modify the JWT token contents, potentially altering user roles, permissions, or other claims to escalate privileges.
assumptions: JWT is not cryptographically signed or is using weak signature

title: Linkability of Authentication Events
description: The authentication service can link multiple authentication events to the same user session via the JWT, potentially creating a detailed profile of user behavior across different services.
assumptions: Authentication service logs and tracks session data

title: Child Identifiability from History Data
description: Child history data retrieved for parent review contains personally identifiable information that could identify the child, including names, dates of events, and potentially sensitive health or behavioral information.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child History
description: Child history data may be accessed by unauthorized parties if the parent user authentication is compromised or if data is transmitted without proper encryption.

title: Parent User Impersonation
description: An unauthorized individual could impersonate the parent user to gain access to child history data, potentially through weak authentication mechanisms or credential theft.

title: Excessive Data Collection in Child History
description: Child history may contain more detailed information than necessary for parent review purposes, including sensitive health, behavioral, or developmental data that exceeds the scope of parental oversight.

title: Linkability of Child History to Other Records
description: Child history data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., medical records, school records, family information) to create a comprehensive profile of the child, increasing privacy risks.
